data.narrative:
Augury is a Series F robotics and manufacturing diagnostics platform that has raised $369M to date. The valuation exercise draws from a universe of 9 private robotics peers (including Locus Robotics, Divergent, Exotec, Generalist AI, and Bedrock Robotics) and 1 public comparable, though direct peer multiples proved insufficiently populated for reliable median-based valuation.

Stage-progression methodology was the primary applicable framework. Using total capital raised ($369M) as a valuation proxy and applying a 1.3x step-up multiplier typical for Series F advancement yields an implied valuation of $480M. This method reflects observed venture step-up patterns across similar-stage deals but does not incorporate company-specific revenue, profitability, or growth metrics. A peer-median approach was not executable; while 10 robotics-sector peers exist, fewer than three share sufficient stage, timing, and valuation-tier alignment to produce statistically meaningful benchmarks.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $408M (low), $480M (median), and $552M (high). The median reflects stage-based progression only. Key uncertainties center on (1) the absence of revenue or bookings data to stress-test growth assumptions, (2) limited same-stage comparable density, and (3) whether public-market robotics comps (1 ticker identified) remain relevant comparators given Augury's private status and specialist positioning. A narrower range would require additional same-stage or revenue-normalized datapoints.
